card.headline: You'll forget *3 out of 4* new words by next week.

beats.speech: You'll forget three out of four new words by next week.
Your brain deletes words on a schedule. Ebbinghaus measured it: about fifty-six percent gone after one hour, sixty-six after a day, seventy-five after six days.
Why? Because you learned the word on its own. Livid equals very angry. A label with nothing to hold it in place, so your brain files it as noise.
Give it a sentence instead. He was livid when his flight was cancelled. A situation plus a feeling: that's a memory anchor.
Better still, learn its whole family, one picture each. Cross: muddy shoes on a clean carpet. Irate: arguing at the service desk.
Fuming: stuck in traffic. Seething: silent, jaw clenched, in a meeting.
Furious: slamming the door. Livid: pale with rage when the flight is cancelled.
Incensed by an unfair headline. Apoplectic: so angry you can't even speak.

card.headline: One word, *eight pictures*.
card.sub: cross → irate → fuming → seething → furious → livid → incensed → apoplectic

beats.speech: One word, eight pictures. Remember one, and you pull up the whole family.

card.headline: Never learn a word *alone*.
card.sub: Look it up · grab 5 synonyms · a picture for each · anotherwordfor.net

beats.speech: Never learn a word alone. Next time, grab five synonyms and a picture for each. Find them in seconds on another word for dot net.
